name: PTC India Ltd
title: PTC India Ltd - 532524 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volumes up 24% to 32.5 BU in Q2 but standalone PBT fell 16% to Rs 152 cr as net surcharge fell Rs 42 cr to Rs 26 cr and no volume guidance was given; supply-side signals are absent.

triggers.label: Net surcharge Rs 42 cr to Rs 26 cr
triggers.quote: Net surcharge income from Rs. 42 crore to Rs. 26 Crores roughly, it has gone down.

triggers.label: No volume guidance for Q3/FY
triggers.quote: Right now we do not have any numbers for the guidance.

triggers.label: Minerals exchange entry
triggers.quote: we are planning to move ahead. Investment is not very big.

red_flags.quote: There is an impairment provision of Rs. 51 crore in this quarter

red_flags.quote: Sir, it is difficult to put up the specific dates as of now.

Right now we do not have any numbers for the guidance.

summary.headline: PTC India Q2 FY27 standalone PAT fell 15% to Rs 113 crore on 24% higher volume, as net surcharge income dropped from Rs 42 crore to Rs 26 crore.
summary.overview: Trading volume rose 24% YoY to 32.5 billion units in Q2 and 18% to 58.2 billion units in H1, led by exchange and medium-term trades. Operating income was flat-to-down (Rs 134 crore vs Rs 137 crore), while PBT fell 15% to Rs 152 crore as net surcharge and treasury income declined after a special dividend reduced cash balances. Consolidated PAT fell 28% to Rs 159 crore, with a Rs 51 crore impairment provision at PTC Financial Services (PFS) a major drag. Management said PFS stake sale is in process with a transaction advisor appointed, but gave no timeline.

segments.name: Power trading (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume 32.5 bn units (+24%); H1 58.2 bn units (+18%), with 60% of H1 volume on exchanges. Q2 trading margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98.

segments.name: Cross-border trade
segments.commentary: Flows to Bangladesh stable with regular payments; Bhutan 1,200 MW winter supply contract signed; Nepal import/export commenced. Lower cross-border income reduced operating income in Q2 as margin is higher than exchange trades.

segments.name: HPX (Hindustan Power Exchange, 22.5% stake)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 18.13 crore vs Rs 9.89 crore YoY; H1 revenue Rs 32.11 crore vs Rs 22.18 crore.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (PFS)
segments.commentary: Q2 impairment provision of Rs 51 crore vs a Rs 57 crore reversal in Q2 FY26; management cited a roughly Rs 40 crore reduction in PFS PAT, which flowed into consolidated numbers.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given for Q3 or full year; management said there is no dramatic change in the current situation.

PFS stake sale: transaction advisor appointed, information dossiers being prepared, nodal officers appointed in PFS; no deadline or dates announced, citing regulatory approvals (RBI, SEBI if required).
Management expects power prices to stay firm in peak hours; intraday price range cited from under Rs 1 to Rs 10 per unit; storage additions expected over the next 12-18 months.
Minerals exchange: planned launch with initial focus on five minerals including iron ore; investment described as modest and funded from cash; partnerships under evaluation.
Dividend: company practice is to declare dividends once a year; no interim dividend expected soon.
Joint venture with NLC: board has met and a business plan is being formulated; near-term (1-2 years) business activity expected to be limited due to connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Solar PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Renewable Energy in the last quarter.
Floated a 500 MW / 2,000 MWh tender for long-term renewable-linked power procurement.
Bhutan winter supply contract of 1,200 MW signed.
Contracted supply to NG delayed by NG itself; safeguards in contract mean no commercial impact, but power has not yet been delivered.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV are early-stage; no capacity or capex figures disclosed.
demand_pricing: Total generation grew 10.64% in H1 while PTC trading volume grew over 18%, which management cited as evidence of market share gains.
Net surcharge income fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore YoY, as DISCOMs paid on time and PTC reduced outstanding dues from a large state utility.
Treasury income fell after a special dividend paid out of the PEL divestment proceeds reduced cash.
Rebate income is netted within sale and purchase account, not shown separately in P&L; management said it depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Gas-based power costs have risen sharply due to Middle East conflict, affecting trading partners' behaviour and RE project timelines.
Market coupling remains pending regulatory directives; HPX competitiveness depends on it.
Minerals trading competitors cited as MSTC and Mjunction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of the PFS stake sale, and is there a deadline?
qa_highlights.answer: Process is on track with a transaction advisor appointed; no deadline or specific dates given because of regulatory approvals and the aim to realise good value after operational stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PAT fall despite higher operating income, and which expense items rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Net surcharge fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore and treasury income fell after the special dividend; establishment costs rose about Rs 2 crore on a base of about Rs 10 crore due to staff transfer from PEL.

qa_highlights.question: What are the trading margins by category?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98; overall about 2.89 paise/unit.

qa_highlights.question: How is rebate income generated and where is it reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebate is earned when a DISCOM does not avail rebate while PTC pays generators early; it is netted within sale and purchase account, not a separate P&L line.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost double QoQ despite large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Includes working capital interest (about Rs 14 crore in H1, Rs 7 crore in Q2) and surcharge expenses paid back-to-back against surcharge income booked in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PTC entering mineral trading and what are the regulatory and competitive issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Synergy with existing 500-600 C&I clients and mining customers; regulator is Indian Bureau of Mines; competitors are MSTC and Mjunction; partnerships being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Can HPX trade given the 5% exchange-trader cap while PTC holds 22.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC does not trade on HPX; trading would require cutting its stake from 22.5% to 5%, a decision still under evaluation.

risks_watch: PFS stake sale: no timeline, and shareholder concerns about the process being delayed or halted; PFS stock trades near 50% of book value per a shareholder question.
Consolidated earnings are exposed to PFS provisions (Rs 51 crore impairment in Q2).
Lower surcharge and treasury income and reliance on rebate income, which depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Recoverability of a previously written-off amount depends on judicial process with no timeline.
Market coupling regulatory directives still awaited; HPX volume outlook depends on it.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV: execution timing uncertain, with connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume growth and cash strength but defensive on PFS divestment, repeatedly declining to give dates or timelines and rejecting shareholder suspicions. Profit decline was attributed to PFS provisions and lower surcharge and treasury income, which management framed as improved receivables management.
key_quotes: Our risk management is far more composed and should that lead to some reduction in the rebate income, still it is much more sustainable than anything else.
The revenue and the trading margin is only a by-product of that, but for some quarters it may go down, for some quarters it may go up.
To divest like a slump sale is not a wise thing. It will not be good for the PTC shareholders also.
There is absolutely no intent on the part of the management to stop in between or create this smoke screen.

adds.what: 1,200 MW solar PPA signed with NTPC Renewable Energy (contracted supply, not company-owned capacity)

growth.why: No revenue or volume guidance was given; management said "we do not have any numbers for the guidance," with Q2 trading volume up 24% but operating income down 2% and standalone PAT down 15%.
